subject: Geography
stem: What is the approximate percentage of carbon in the Earth's crust?
exp: The crust is overwhelmingly oxygen (~46%) and silicon (~28%), then aluminium, iron, calcium, etc.; carbon is only a trace element (~0.02–0.025% by weight), held mostly in carbonate rocks and fossil fuels. 0.025% is the accepted value; 0.045% overstates it and 0.015%/0.005% understate it.

subject: Geography
stem: Arrange the following major elements present in the Earth's crust, in ascending order, in weight percentage
exp: By weight, Oxygen (~46.6%) > Silicon (~27.7%) > Aluminium (~8.1%) > Calcium (~3.6%). Ascending (smallest first) is Calcium → Aluminium → Silicon → Oxygen = 2,1,3,4. The other codes break this fixed order — oxygen and silicon are always the two largest and must come last.
subs: 1. Aluminium
2. Calcium
3. Silicon
4. Oxygen

subject: Geography
stem: Xeriscaping is a concept related to
options: landscaping related to save soil erosion
exp: Xeriscaping (Greek xeros = dry) uses drought-tolerant plants, mulching and efficient design to minimise irrigation — water-saving gardening for dry regions. It is unrelated to soil-erosion control or rock weathering, so b and c (and therefore "All of the above") are wrong.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is a type of igneous rock?
exp: Rocks are classed by origin — igneous from cooled magma/lava, sedimentary from compacted sediments, metamorphic from heat/pressure alteration. Granite is a coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock formed by slow underground cooling (hence large crystals). Marble is metamorphic (altered limestone), Halite a sedimentary evaporite (rock salt), Shale a sedimentary rock of compacted clay.

stem: Identify the type of drainage pattern on the basis of the given characteristics:
exp: A dendritic pattern (Greek dendron = tree) develops on uniform rock with no structural control, so streams branch freely like tree limbs/leaf veins, meeting at acute angles — the commonest natural pattern. Radial drains outward from a dome/volcano, trellis forms on folded hard–soft rock (right-angle junctions), centripetal drains inward into a basin.
subs: 1. It represents the most common pattern of streams and their tributaries
2. It occurs in areas of uniform rock type and regular slope

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements with reference to Salt Weathering is/are correct?
exp: Salt weathering shatters rock as salts in pore water crystallise and expand. Crystallisation is the most powerful of these mechanisms (1 true), and it works best on porous rock — sedimentary types like sandstone/limestone soak up salty water more than dense granite, so they break down faster (2 true).
subs: 1. Salt crystallisation is the most effective of all the salt weathering processes.
2. Salt crystal growth is more effective over sedimentary rocks as compared to igneous rocks.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements with regard to volcanoes is not correct?
options: Stratovolcanoes produce lava flows that initially follow valleys but are highly resistant to erosion.
The surrounding areas can remain highlands, lava ridges or mesas.
Hawaiian shield volcanoes are eroded by streams that form deeply carved valleys with steeply sloping heads.
The system of streams on a dissected volcano cone is not a radial drainage pattern.
exp: Water running down a cone's slopes spreads outward in all directions, giving a classic radial pattern — so "not radial" is false. The others correctly note that resistant lava forms ridges/mesas and that streams dissect shield volcanoes.

subject: Geography
stem: Extrusive volcanoes are not found in which one of the following mountains?
exp: Surface (extrusive) volcanism concentrates along plate margins, especially the Pacific "Ring of Fire." The Himalayas are young fold mountains raised by the India–Eurasia collision (crust crumpling, not magma erupting), so they have no volcanoes. The Alaskan, Rocky and Andean belts lie on the active Pacific margin.

subject: Geography
stem: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists
exp: Merapi is on Indonesia's Sunda arc; Sakurajima erupts almost continuously in southern Japan; Vesuvius (Naples, Italy) buried Pompeii in 79 CE; Mauna Loa is Hawaii's giant basaltic shield. So A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1; the other codes wrongly move Sakurajima/Vesuvius out of Japan/Italy.
subs: List-I (Active Volcano)
A. Mount Merapi
B. Sakurajima

D. Mauna Loa
List-II (Location)
1. Hawaii
2. Italy

4. Indonesia

subject: Geography
stem: Individual lava flows are normally only a few feet thick, but over a long period of time, repeated flows may build up a volcano. Such volcanoes are termed as
exp: Thin, fluid basaltic lava spreads far and stacks flow on flow to build a broad, gently sloping shield volcano (e.g. Mauna Loa). Composite/strato-volcanoes are steep cones of alternating lava and ash from explosive eruptions, and cinder cones are small pyroclastic mounds — none built mainly of thin repeated flows.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements about volcanoes are correct?
exp: The Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) rates eruption magnitude (1). Iceland (Mid-Atlantic Ridge) and the Philippine island arc are volcanic in origin (2). Weathered lava/ash gives deep, mineral-rich soils supporting intensive farming, as in Java (3). All three are correct.
subs: 1. The strength of a volcano is measured by the Volcanic Explosive Index.
2. Iceland and Philippines were created by volcanic activity.
3. Volcanic soils are rich, deep and fertile and allow intensive agriculture to take place.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements regarding Arc Volcanoes is/are correct?
exp: Arc volcanoes form where one plate subducts under another — at convergent boundaries — so statement 1 (divergent) is wrong. Subduction builds steep stratovolcanoes like Fuji and Mayon (2), and the Andean arc holds the highest volcano, Ojos del Salado (3).
subs: 1. Arc volcanoes are found near divergent plate boundaries.
2. Some of the world's classical examples of cone-shaped stratovolcanoes, such as Mount Fuji in Japan, Mayon in the Philippines are Arc volcanoes.
3. Some of the highest volcanoes on Earth are of the Arc type, notably Nevado Ojos del Salado in the Chilean Andes.

subject: Geography
stem: With reference to earthquakes, which of the following statements are correct?
exp: Quakes cluster at converging/transform margins where locked rocks snap (1). The underground rupture point is the focus/hypocentre; the surface point above it is the epicentre, and shaking fades away from it (2, 3). Statement 4 is false — most epicentres actually lie over oceans, along oceanic plate boundaries.
subs: 1. Earthquakes largely occur along the converging plate boundaries.
2. Point of origin of earthquake in lithosphere is known as focus (hypocentre).
3. Intensity of earthquake decreases with distance from the epicentre.
4. Epicentre of earthquake always remains over continents only.

subject: Geography
stem: Tsunami waves are the undersea occurrence of earthquake exceeding 7.5 on Richter scale. Which one of the following statements regarding this is not correct?
options: The pacific coasts are most vulnerable to Tsunami waves.
Tsunami waves are also called high-energy tidal waves or seismic sea waves.
exp: "Tsunami" is Japanese (tsu = harbour, nami = wave), not Latin. The others are correct — seafloor displacement makes powerful long waves, the seismically active Pacific rim is most exposed, and "seismic sea wave" is an alternative name.

subject: Geography
stem: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists
exp: Lakes are named by basin origin. Bhimtal sits in a tectonic depression (3), Ashtamudi (Kerala) is a coastal lagoon (1), Gohna formed when a landslide dammed a valley (2), and Lonar fills a meteorite crater (4). So A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4.

exp: Bhimtal is a tectonic-basin lake (4), Lonar a meteorite-crater lake (1), Gangabal (Kashmir) a glacial cirque lake (2), and Purbasthali (West Bengal) an ox-bow — a fluvial lake (3). So A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not a major tectonic plate?
options: Antarctica and the surrounding oceanic plate
exp: The seven major plates are Pacific, North American, South American, Eurasian, African, Antarctic and Indo-Australian. The Arabian ("Saudi Arabian") plate is a small minor plate between the African and Eurasian plates, so it is not a major plate; the others name parts of major plates.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements about primary waves of earthquakes is not correct?
options: They are similar to sound waves.
They can travel only through solid materials.
They travel through gaseous, liquid and solid materials.
They move faster and are the first to arrive at the surface.
exp: P-waves are longitudinal (compressional) waves, like sound, and crucially pass through all media — solids, liquids and gases (they even cross the liquid outer core). So "only through solids" is false. They are the fastest waves and arrive first (those statements are correct).

subject: Geography
stem: Who amongst the following will be at more risk with respect to the earthquake hazard zone specified by the Geological Survey of India?
exp: India's seismic zones run II–V by rising hazard; the young, active Himalayas are Zone V (very high). Pithoragarh lies in this Himalayan Zone V, so Malti faces the greatest risk. Indore is Zone III and Secunderabad/Bhubaneswar are Zones II–III.

subject: Geography
stem: The extent of damage caused by earthquake is not in uenced by which one of the following?
exp: Damage depends on the energy released (magnitude), the number of people/structures exposed (density), and how quake-resistant the buildings are. Climate has no bearing on how much a quake destroys, so it is the exception.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the other term used for Focus in relation with an earthquake?
exp: The focus is the point inside the Earth where rupture begins; its synonym is the hypocentre. The epicentre is the surface point above the focus; "isocentre" and "principal point" are not seismological terms.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements regarding river meanders is/are correct?
exp: A meander is a loop formed by lateral erosion on a floodplain (1). A tight gooseneck loop can be pinched off in a flood, leaving an oxbow lake (2). If the land rises, the river cuts down while keeping its bends, giving incised meanders (3). All three are correct.
subs: 1. It is a U-shaped bend in a river.
2. An extremely tight meander is called a gooseneck it is likely to become a cutoff, or oxbow lake, after aflood.
3. Tectonic uplift can cause a river to continue downcutting along its meandering course, producing incised or entrenched meanders.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements regarding S-waves is not correct?
options: During an earthquake S-waves are less destructive to structures like buildings and highway overpasses.
S-waves can travel only through solids and cannot travel through the Earth's outer core.
Seismologists have concluded that the Earth's outer core must be liquid or fluid.
exp: S-waves (shear waves) shake the ground sideways and are in fact more destructive to buildings than P-waves, so "less destructive" is wrong. The others are true: S-waves are slower, pass only through solids, and their inability to cross the outer core is the proof that it is liquid.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements with reference to Richter scale is/are correct?
exp: Richter is a magnitude scale — it measures the energy released at the source (each step ≈ 32× more energy), so statement 2 is correct. Intensity (felt shaking/damage at a place) is measured by the Mercalli scale, so statement 1 is wrong.
subs: 1. It is the intensity scale of an earthquake.
2. Richter indicates the amount of energy released during the earthquake.
Select the answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not related to wind erosion?
exp: Zeugen (tabular rock ridges) and dreikanter (wind-faceted pebbles) are aeolian features. A demoiselle (earth pillar) is a soft-rock column capped by a boulder, carved by rain-wash, not wind. (A "wind gap" is also not truly wind-erosion, but the demoiselle is the intended answer.)

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct?
exp: Snow- and glacier-fed Himalayan rivers are perennial (they flow even in winter), so statement 1 is wrong. Peninsular rivers on old hard rock have graded their valleys (maturity, 2), and long Himalayan rivers pass through youthful, mature and old stages along their course (3).
subs: 1. Himalayan rivers have their origin in the snow-covered areas, hence are dry in winter season.
2. Rivers of the Peninsular Plateau have reached maturity.
3. Himalayan rivers depict all the three stages of normal cycle of erosion.
Select the correct answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Statement I: Portions of glacial troughs may exhibit remarkably flat floor.
options: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
Both the statements are individually true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
exp: A glacial trough is the broad U-shaped valley a glacier carves; its floor is often flat because the heavy, broad-based ice grinds the bottom evenly across its width. So statement II (uniform glacial erosion) is exactly why the floor is flat — a valid cause-and-effect.
subs: Statement II: The flat floor in a glacial trough is produced by uniform glacial erosion.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following river valleys of India is under the influence of intensive gully erosion?
exp: Gully erosion carves deep channels into soft soil, forming badland "ravines"; the Chambal valley is the classic example, full of ravines. The Kosi is known for shifting/flooding, the Damodar historically for floods, and the Brahmaputra for braiding and bank erosion — not gully ravines.

subject: Geography
stem: The term soil impoverishment relates to which one of the following?
options: Soil getting very deficient in plant nutrients
Soil getting enriched with plant nutrients
exp: Impoverishment is loss of fertility — repeated cropping or leaching strips out nitrogen, phosphorus and other nutrients. It differs from erosion/deposition (which move soil physically) and is the opposite of enrichment.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following landforms is/are formed by wind erosion?
exp: A zeugen is a hard-rock cap left on a softer pedestal after wind erodes around it — a desert (aeolian) feature. A cirque is glacial and a stack is coastal (marine erosion), so only zeugen is wind-formed.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not an example of chemical weathering?
exp: Chemical weathering alters minerals through reactions — acid action, hydrolysis (with water) and oxidation (with oxygen, e.g. rusting). Salt crystal growth breaks rock by the physical pressure of crystals in pores, so it is mechanical, not chemical.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements with regard to the Indian Railways is not correct?
options: The Indian rail networks have been developed throughout the Konkan coast.
There is very low density of railway lines in the Himalayan region.
The north Indian plain has a dense network of railway.
At present, India has the largest railway network in the world.
exp: By route length India's network is among the largest but ranks about fourth (after the USA, China, Russia), so "largest in the world" is false. The Konkan Railway, sparse Himalayan lines, and dense northern-plain network are all correct.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements in respect to the Indian Peninsular Plateau are correct?
exp: The Deccan generally rises toward the south (1), the Satpura range lies between the Narmada and Tapi (3), and Chota Nagpur is old Archaean granite/gneiss (4). Statement 2 is wrong — the Malwa Plateau is in the north-west and does not form the eastern flank.
subs: 1. The Deccan Plateau gradually rises from North to South.
2. The Malwa Plateau dominates the Vindhyan scarps, forming the Eastern ank of the plateau.
3. The Western Satpuras separate the Narmada and Tapi rivers.
4. The Chota Nagpur Plateau is composed of Archaean granite and gneiss rocks.
Select the correct answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Statement I: By far the most common topographic form in a Karst terrain is the sinkhole.
options: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
Both the statements are individually true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
exp: Karst forms where acidic water dissolves limestone, and sinkholes are its commonest surface form (I true). It is also true they range widely in depth (II true). But describing their depth does not explain why they are the most common form, so II is not the explanation.
subs: Statement II: Topographically, sinkhole is depression that varies in depth from less than a meter to few hundred meters.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not a uvial landform?
exp: Gorges and canyons are deep river-cut valleys, and braids are interlacing river channels — all fluvial. A cirque is an armchair hollow gouged by a mountain glacier, so it is glacial.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched? Plateau - Continent
exp: The Abyssinian Plateau is in Ethiopia, Africa (1), and the Anatolian Plateau is in Turkey, Asia (3). Patagonia is in South America (not Australia) and the Iberian Meseta is in Europe (not North America), so 2 and 4 are wrong.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding barrier islands is/are correct?
exp: Barrier islands are long sand ridges lying parallel and close to the shore, enclosing a lagoon/marsh (2), and being low and shifting they are easily overrun in storms (3). Statement 1 is wrong on the detail "far from the coast" — they form just offshore.
subs: 1. These are small chain of sand islands that form offshore, far from the coast.
2. Lagoons or shallower marshes separate the barrier islands from the mainland.
3. Such locations are hazardous for settlements because they are easily swept away by storms and hurricanes.

subject: Geography
stem: Amsterdam-St. Paul Plateau is located in which one of the following oceanic regions?
exp: It is a submarine volcanic plateau around Île Amsterdam and Île Saint-Paul in the southern Indian Ocean (French sub-Antarctic territory), far from the Arctic, Atlantic and Pacific.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements with reference to Glacial trough is/are correct?
exp: Valley glaciers scrape away loose cover and gouge bedrock into a U-shaped trough (1). Where that trough was cut below sea level, the sea floods it after the ice melts, drowning the valley as a fjord (2). Both are correct.
subs: 1. Alpine glaciers strip valleys of their soil, regolith and sediment to form glacial troughs.
2. When the sea level is below the floor of a glacial trough, the seawater enters as the ice front recedes, creating a ord.
Select the answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements concerning atmosphere of the Earth are correct?
exp: Temperature behaves differently in each layer. In the stratosphere it rises with height because ozone absorbs UV (1). In the mesosphere it falls with height (2), bottoming out at the mesopause (upper mesosphere) — the coldest part of the atmosphere (3). The tropopause, the boundary above the troposphere, has near-constant temperature (isothermal, 4). All four are correct.
subs: 1. In stratosphere, temperature increases with altitude.
2. In mesosphere, temperature decreases with altitude.
3. The lowest temperature of the atmosphere is recorded in the upper part of mesosphere.
4. Tropopause is an isothermal zone.
Select the correct answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Most ozone gas (about 90%) is located in the atmospheric layer of
exp: About 90% of atmospheric ozone forms the ozone layer in the stratosphere (~15–35 km up), where it absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation. Very little ozone exists in the lower troposphere or in the higher mesosphere/ionosphere.

subject: Geography
stem: Statement I: Global warming signi es the rise in global surface temperature.
options: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
Both the statements are individually true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
exp: Global warming is indeed the rise in average surface temperature (I). Greenhouse gases (CO₂, methane, etc.) trap outgoing heat, and their build-up is precisely why temperatures rise (II). So II is the direct cause of I — a valid assertion–reason pair.
subs: Statement II: The increase of concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere causes the rise in global surface temperature.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following causes adiabatic temperature changes in atmosphere?
options: Expansion and compression of the air
Partial absorption of solar radiation by the atmosphere
exp: An "adiabatic" change is one with no heat exchange with the surroundings. As air rises into lower pressure it expands and cools; as it sinks it is compressed and warms — purely from pressure change. Latent heat and solar absorption involve actual heat gain/loss, so they are non-adiabatic.

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following constituent gases of the atmosphere
exp: By volume the order is Argon (~0.93%) > CO₂ (~0.04%) > Neon (~0.0018%) > Helium (~0.0005%). A true ascending list would be Helium-Neon-CO₂-Argon (3-2-4-1), which isn't offered; option b is exactly this correct magnitude order written in descending form, so the question's "ascending" label looks like a misprint. Among the choices, only b reflects the real abundances.
subs: 1. Argon
2. Neon
3. Helium
4. Carbon dioxide Which one of the following is the correct ascending sequence of the above gases in terms of the volume percentage?

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements with regard to ozone is not correct?
options: Ozone is found mostly at 15-55 km in the atmosphere.
Ozone is produced by gaseous chemical reactions.
16th November is celebrated as the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.
Ozone is a form of oxygen in which three oxygen atoms are bounded together.
exp: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is 16 September (marking the Montreal Protocol), not 16 November — so this is the wrong statement. Ozone (O₃) does occur mainly in the stratosphere, forms by photochemical reactions, and is the three-atom form of oxygen.

subject: Geography
stem: Ozone layer, which absorbs the ultra-violet radiation, is found in which one of the following layers of the atmosphere?
exp: The UV-shielding ozone layer lies in the stratosphere. The troposphere is the weather layer below it; the mesosphere and ionosphere lie far above and hold little ozone.

subject: Geography
stem: How much percentage of carbon dioxide is present in the atmosphere of Venus and Mars?
exp: Both Venus and Mars have atmospheres made almost entirely of carbon dioxide (~96%). The lower percentages are far too small for these CO₂-dominated atmospheres.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements regarding insolation is/are correct?
exp: Incoming solar radiation (insolation) is mostly short-wave energy in the visible band (1, correct). Statement 2 reverses cause and effect — the Earth's curvature makes insolation uneven (the slanting rays near the poles spread over a larger area, so they receive less). Hence 1 only.
subs: 1. Insolation is predominantly short-wave radiation, with wavelengths in the range of 0.39 micrometre to 0.76 micrometre.
2. Insolation is evenly distributed across the Earth because of the Earth's curved surface.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

subject: Geography
stem: Which greenhouse gas has maximum average residence time in the atmosphere?
exp: Residence time is how long a gas persists. CFCs are extremely stable and last for many decades to over a century — far longer than methane (~12 years) or water vapour (days). Hence CFCs have the longest residence time among these.

subject: Geography
stem: Ozone hole is a region over
options: the Antarctic caused mainly by CFC gases
the Antarctic caused mainly by carbon dioxide gas
the Arctic caused mainly by CFC gases
the Arctic caused mainly by carbon dioxide gas
exp: The ozone "hole" is the severe seasonal thinning over Antarctica, where extreme cold and polar stratospheric clouds let chlorine from CFCs destroy ozone efficiently. It is not over the Arctic, and CO₂ is not the cause.

subject: Geography
stem: The Kyoto Protocol specifically relates to which one among the following issues?
exp: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) bound industrialised countries to cut greenhouse-gas emissions. Ozone/CFCs are handled by the Montreal Protocol and biodiversity by the Convention on Biological Diversity.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the largest source of electricity in India?
exp: Coal-based thermal plants generate the bulk of India's electricity (well over half). Hydropower is the next largest; nuclear and wind contribute much smaller shares.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements with regard to Jet stream, an upper level tropospheric wave, is not correct?
options: It is a narrow band of high-velocity wind.
It follows the wave path near the tropopause at elevations of 8 km to 15 km.
Jet streams are typically continuous over long distances.
In summer, the polar front jet achieves its maximum force.
exp: The polar-front jet is strongest in winter, when the temperature contrast between polar and tropical air is greatest; it weakens in summer — so "maximum force in summer" is wrong. The descriptions of jets as narrow, fast, continuous bands near the tropopause are correct.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following may be the true characteristic of cyclones?
options: Temperate cyclones move from west to east with westerlies whereas tropical cyclones follow trade winds.
The front side of cyclone is known as the eye of cyclone.
Cyclones possess a centre of high pressure surrounded by closed isobars.
Hurricanes are well-known tropical cyclones which develop over mid-latitudes.
exp: Temperate (mid-latitude) cyclones are steered eastward by the westerlies, whereas tropical cyclones are carried by the easterly trade winds — option a is correct. A cyclone's eye is at its centre (not the front), its centre is low pressure (not high), and hurricanes form over warm tropical seas (not mid-latitudes).

subject: Geography
stem: In the region of eastern shore of Adriatic Sea, a cold and dry wind blowing down from the mountain is known as
exp: The Bora is a cold, dry katabatic wind that rushes down to the eastern Adriatic coast (Croatia). The Mistral blows down the Rhône valley in France, the Bise is a cold Alpine/Swiss wind, and a blizzard is a snowstorm — none specific to the Adriatic.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following are warm ocean currents?
options: North Atlantic Drift and Brazil Current
West Wind Drift and Falkland Current
exp: Warm currents carry tropical water polewards along western sides of oceans/eastern coasts. Both the North Atlantic Drift and the Brazil Current are warm. Each other pair contains a cold current — California, Canaries/Benguela, West Wind Drift/Falkland are all cold.

subject: Geography
stem: In the Hadley cell thermal circulation, air rises up and finally descends at
exp: In the Hadley cell, heated equatorial air rises (at the ITCZ/doldrums), moves poleward aloft, and sinks at about 30° latitude, forming the subtropical high-pressure belts (the source of trade winds and the world's hot deserts). The ITCZ/equatorial trough is the rising limb, not where air descends.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements about the Coriolis force is not correct?
options: It is maximum at the Poles.
It is absent at the Equator.
It deflects the wind to the right direction in the southern hemisphere.
It deflects the wind to the right direction in the northern hemisphere.
exp: The Coriolis force (from Earth's rotation) deflects moving air to the left in the southern hemisphere and to the right in the northern hemisphere — so statement c is wrong. It is indeed zero at the equator and greatest at the poles.

subject: Geography
stem: Manikaran in Himachal Pradesh is known for
exp: Manikaran is famous for its hot springs and geothermal potential, where underground heat brings boiling water to the surface. It is not a solar, bio- or wind-energy site.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not a resultant of the El Ni�o effect?
options: Flow of the South-East Trade Winds towards the Indian Ocean
Irregularities in the evaporation of sea water
Reduction in the amount of planktons which reduces the number offish in the sea
exp: During El Niño the Pacific trade winds weaken or reverse (warm water shifts east toward South America), so a normal flow of South-East Trades toward the Indian Ocean is not an El Niño outcome. The genuine effects are disrupted circulation, altered evaporation, and a crash in plankton/fish off Peru.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following do not influence the ocean currents?
options: Gravitational pull by Sun and Moon
exp: Currents are driven by uneven solar heating, prevailing winds, and the Coriolis deflection. The gravitational pull of the Sun and Moon causes tides (the rise and fall of sea level), not the horizontal flow of currents.

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following statements
options: Both the statements are correct and statement 2 is the correct explanation of statement 1.
Both the statements are correct, but statement 2 is not the correct explanation of statement 1.
Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false, but statement 2 is correct.
exp: Hadley cells are the great tropical overturning loops that set up the trade winds and subtropical highs — central to global wind patterns (1). They exist because intense equatorial heating makes air rise and circulate (2). So statement 2 explains why Hadley cells exist, underpinning statement 1.
subs: 1. Hadley cells are key to understanding the wind patterns of Earth.

2. Hadley cells are formed because the Equator is heated more strongly by the Sun than other places, creating thermal circulations. With regard to the statements given above, which of the following is correct?

subject: Geography
stem: With reference to the continent of Antarctica which of the following statements are correct?
exp: Antarctica (~14 million km²) is larger than Europe (1) and, due to its thick ice sheet, has the highest mean elevation of any continent (2). Statement 3 is wrong — its highest peak is the Vinson Massif, not Mt Ross — and statement 4 is wrong — the West Wind Drift (Antarctic Circumpolar Current) flows clockwise (west to east) around the continent.
subs: 1. It is larger than Europe in terms of area.
2. It has the highest average elevation as compared to all other continents.
3. Mt. Ross is the highest peak of this continent.
4. Waters of the Southern Ocean West Wind Drift move in an anticlockwise direction around it.
Select the answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: The pattern of planetary winds largely depends upon which of the following factors?
exp: The global wind belts are shaped by uneven heating by latitude (which creates pressure belts), by the unequal heating of land vs sea (which distorts those belts), and by Earth's rotation (the Coriolis effect that bends the winds). All three factors apply.
subs: 1. Latitudinal variation of atmospheric heating
2. The distribution of continents and oceans
3. The rotation of earth
Select the answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Identify the climate type based on the given characteristics
exp: A strong winter anticyclone (like the Siberian High) that brings dry winters, with summer rain from a monsoon-like reversal and cool summers, describes the cold continental climate with dry winters (Köppen Dw, e.g. Manchuria/Siberia margins). A subtropical steppe or humid subtropical type lacks this winter anticyclone, and tundra has no such monsoon-like reversal.
subs: 1. The annual precipitation is low and is around 15 cm.
2. The development of pronounced winter anticyclones and their weakening in summer sets in monsoon-like reversal of wind in this region.
3. Polewards, summer temperatures are low.
Select the answer from the options given below

subject: Geography
stem: South Arcot and Ramanathapuram receive over 50 percent of their annual rainfall from which one of the following?
options: Bay of Bengal branch of summer monsoon
exp: These Tamil Nadu districts lie on the south-eastern coast, in the rain-shadow of the south-west monsoon. They get most of their rain from the retreating (north-east) monsoon of October–December, when winds pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and strike the Coromandel coast.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following States receives rainfall from both the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch of Monsoon?
exp: In the north-west, the Bay of Bengal branch (deflected up the Ganga plain) and the Arabian Sea branch converge over Punjab, so it gets rain from both. Maharashtra is fed mainly by the Arabian Sea branch, Meghalaya by the Bay branch, and Tamil Nadu chiefly by the north-east monsoon.

subject: Geography
stem: Identify the type of climate on the basis of the following characteristics relating to it
exp: High year-round temperatures with a short rainy season and a long dry season define the tropical wet-and-dry (savanna, Aw) climate — often called the "Sudan type." Steppe climates are semi-arid grasslands, and the tropical monsoon climate has heavier, more concentrated rainfall.
subs: I. Temperature is high throughout the year. II. Rainfall is variable with a short wet season and a longer dry season. III. Climate of Sudan and Paraguay is an example of this climate type.
Select the answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: The Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) launched in 2015-16 by the Central Government is aimed to
options: make agriculture more modern and globally competitive.
provide improved access to irrigation and enhanced water efficiency.
support promotion of organic farming in the country.
reduce dependence of agriculture on monsoon.
exp: PKVY promotes organic farming through a cluster-based approach, certification and market linkage. Irrigation/water efficiency is the focus of PMKSY, so the other options describe different schemes.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following countries had chosen the name Nisarga for the cyclone which devastated the coastline of Maharashtra and Gujarat in June 2020?
exp: Cyclone names are drawn in rotation from lists submitted by member countries of the regional panel; "Nisarga" was the name contributed by Bangladesh.

stem: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists
exp: The same tropical storm has regional names: cyclone in the Indian Ocean (3), hurricane in the Atlantic (4), typhoon in the South China Sea/NW Pacific (2), and willy-willy in Western Australia (1). So A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1.

subject: Geography
stem: Tuvalu has become a point of discussion recently. Why?
options: Potato plant that could grow in high altitude
Place in equatorial Africa, where snow is found
New innovative technology to meet global warming
A country under threat of submergence due to ice melting and sea level rise
exp: Tuvalu is a low-lying Pacific island nation barely above sea level, so it is repeatedly in the news as one of the countries most at risk of submergence from climate-driven sea-level rise. The other options are unrelated.

subject: Geography
stem: Statement I: In Tundra climate, biodiversity is comparatively less.
options: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
Both the statements are individually true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
exp: The tundra's intense cold and very short growing/warm season give organisms little time to grow and reproduce, so few species survive — low biodiversity (I). Statement II (the short warm/reproductive period) is the very reason for that low diversity, so it explains I.
subs: Statement II: Tundra climate has less reproductive warm period.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following regions is an important supplier of citrus fruits?
exp: The Mediterranean climate — warm, dry summers and mild, wet winters — is ideal for oranges, lemons and other citrus, making this region a leading citrus supplier. Equatorial, desert and sub-humid regions are not noted citrus belts.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following indicates the Tropical Savannah climate?
exp: In Köppen's system, "A" = tropical and "w" = dry winter, so Aw is tropical savanna (wet summer, dry winter). Dfc is subarctic, Cwg a dry-winter subtropical type, and Am tropical monsoon.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following cities is closest to the Equator?
exp: Singapore lies at about 1.3°N, the nearest to the equator. Mogadishu (~2°N), Colombo (~6.9°N) and Manila (~14.6°N) are all farther away.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is a cold ocean current?
exp: The California Current is a cold current flowing south along the western coast of North America (an eastern boundary current). The Brazilian Current, Gulf Stream and North Equatorial Current are all warm.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following climatic types (K�ppen's Scheme) is best suited to describe the climate of the western fringe of Rajasthan?
exp: Western Rajasthan (the Thar) is a hot desert; in Köppen, "B" = dry, "W" = desert, "h" = hot — so BWhw fits. Aw/Amw are tropical wet types and Cwg is a humid subtropical type, none matching a hot desert.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one among the following State capitals is closest to the Equator?
exp: Panaji (Goa) lies at about 15.5°N, the nearest to the equator among these. Hyderabad (~17.4°N), Mumbai (~19°N) and Bhubaneswar (~20.3°N) are farther north.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements regarding ice-cap climate is/are correct?
exp: The ice-cap (frost) climate is Köppen EF (1) and is the harshest climate, with every month below freezing (2) — found over Antarctica and Greenland. Statement 3 is wrong; the Pir Panjal/Great Himalayas have highland (mountain) climates, not the permanent ice-cap type.
subs: 1. In the K�ppen climate classification, the ice-cap climate is signi ed by the letters EF.
2. It is the Earth's most severe climate, where the mean monthly temperature is never above 0 degree Celsius.
3. This climate is found in the Pir Panjal and the Great Himalayas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

subject: Geography
stem: What does BW stand for as per the K�ppen climate classification?
exp: In Köppen's scheme "B" denotes dry climates; BW is the desert (arid) type and BS is the steppe (semi-arid) type. Tundra is "ET" and mesothermal climates are the "C" group.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct?
exp: Every point completes one rotation in 24 hours, so angular velocity is uniform everywhere (1). But points at the equator trace a far bigger circle than points near the poles in the same time, so their linear (surface) speed is greatest at the equator and nil at the poles (2). Both are correct.
subs: 1. Angular velocity for all locations on the Earth's surface is the same while linear velocity varies.
2. Linear velocity is maximum at the equator and minimum at the poles.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements with reference to lines of latitudes is/are correct?
exp: Because the Earth is slightly flattened (an oblate spheroid), the ground distance for one degree of latitude changes a little from equator to pole (1). Counting parallels at 1° intervals gives 89 in each hemisphere plus the equator = 179 (the two poles are points, not parallels) (2). Both correct.
subs: 1. The distance between two successive latitudes changes slightly from the equator to the poles.
2. If parallels of latitude are drawn at an interval of one degree, the total number of parallels thus drawn, including the equator, will be 179.
Select the answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following statements with reference to Mid-latitude deciduous forests
exp: Deciduous trees shed their leaves in autumn/winter (to survive the cold), not summer — so statement 1 is wrong. They are native to eastern North America and Western Europe (2), in Asia lie between the boreal forest and the steppes (3), and include beech, hickory and walnut (4). Hence 2, 3 and 4.
subs: 1. Mid-latitude deciduous forests consist largely of trees that drop their leaves during the summer season.
2. Mid-latitude deciduous forests are native to eastern North America and Western Europe.
3. In Asia, the Mid-latitude deciduous forests occur as a belt between the boreal forest to the north and steppe lands to the south.
4. Beech, Hickory and Walnut are common examples of trees found in Mid-latitude deciduous forests. Which of the statements given above are correct?

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following pairs with reference to world climate types and their characteristics Climate Characteristic
exp: Pair I is right (tropical wet-and-dry has a dry winter) and pair III is right (humid continental — no dry season, warm summer). Pair II is wrong — a steppe is semi-arid, not humid. Pair IV is wrong — a marine west-coast climate has mild, not "severely cold," summers. So 2 pairs match.
subs: I. Tropical wet and Winter dry season dry II. Sub-tropical steppe Humid III. Mid-latitude No dry season, warm summer No dry season, severely cold IV. Marine west coast summer How many of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements with regard to the winter solstice is correct?
options: The South Pole experiences 24 hours of darkness.
The North Pole experiences 24 hours of darkness.
exp: At the (Northern) winter solstice (~22 Dec) the North Pole is tilted away from the Sun and stays dark for 24 hours, while the South Pole has continuous daylight. It occurs in December (not June), and Earth is near perihelion (closest to the Sun) in early January, not aphelion.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following about sugar industry of Peninsular India is not correct?
options: High yield per hectare of sugarcane
Most of the mills in the Peninsula are located mainly along the east coast
exp: The peninsula's advantages come from its cooler maritime climate — higher cane yields, higher sucrose, and a longer crushing season. The claim that most mills lie along the east coast is the incorrect/odd statement (mills are spread across the interior cane belts, not concentrated on the east coast).

subject: Geography
stem: Statement I: The interior part of Maharashtra does not receive adequate rain in the summer season.
options: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
Both the statements are individually true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
exp: The Western Ghats force the moist Arabian Sea monsoon to drop most of its rain on the windward (western) side; the interior on the leeward side gets little — the classic rain-shadow effect. So statement II is exactly why interior Maharashtra is dry (statement I).
subs: Statement II: The interior part of Maharashtra lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats.

subject: Geography
stem: Tropical evergreen rain forest biome provides optimum environmental conditions for the growth of plants and animals. Which one among the following statements regarding this is not correct?
options: It has heavy rainfall and high temperature throughout the year.
This biome is also called megathe rmal biome.
The evergreen rain forest biome extends between 10�N and 10�S latitudes.
The maximum development of this biome has taken place in central and southern California, and northwestern coastal lands of Africa.
exp: California and NW Africa have Mediterranean climates, not rainforest — so statement d is false. Tropical rainforest has hot, wet conditions year-round, is "megathermal," and lies in the equatorial belt (~10°N–10°S), as in the Amazon and Congo.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements with regard to cloudburst is/are correct?
exp: A cloudburst is a sudden, intense, localized downpour (1) that occurs mostly over hilly terrain (where rising air triggers it) (2), dumping very high rainfall in a short time (3). Statement 4 is wrong — cloudbursts are not restricted to daytime. Hence 1, 2 and 3.
subs: 1. It is defined as sudden localized very heavy downpour with cloud thunder and lightning.
2. It mostly occurs in the hilly areas.
3. It results into very high intensity of rainfall, i.e., 250 mm-300 mm in a couple of hours.
4. It occurs only during daytime.
Select the correct answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements related to latitude are true?
exp: Climate elements shift with latitude (1); day-length difference grows toward the poles (near the equator days are nearly equal, near the poles you get 24-hour days/nights) (2); and Indira Point, India's southernmost tip, lies at about 6°45′N (3). All three are correct.
subs: 1. Rainfall, temperature and vegetation vary with latitude.
2. The difference between the longest day and the shortest day increases with latitude.
3. Indira Point is located approximately at 6�45'N latitude.
Select the correct answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is applicable to collision-coalescence process of precipitation?
options: Clouds which do not extend beyond the freezing level
Clouds which extend beyond the freezing level
exp: Collision-coalescence is the "warm rain" mechanism: in clouds whose tops stay below 0 °C, larger droplets fall faster, collide with smaller ones and merge into raindrops. Clouds reaching above the freezing level rely on the ice-crystal (Bergeron) process instead.

subject: Geography
stem: Atmospheric conditions are well-governed by humidity. Which one among the following may best define humidity?
options: Form of suspended water droplets caused by condensation
Almost microscopically small drops of water condensed from and suspended in air
The moisture content of the atmosphere at a particular time and place
exp: Humidity is simply the amount of water vapour present in the air at a given time and place. The other options describe fog, dew or cloud droplets — which are condensation (water in liquid form), not the vapour content itself.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not a geographical requirement for cultivation of cotton?
options: Temperature reaching 25�C or more in summer
Medium loam soil with good drainage
A growing period of at least 100 frost free days
exp: Cotton actually needs about 200+ frost-free days to mature, so "at least 100" understates the requirement — that is the wrong condition. High summer warmth, moderate rainfall and well-drained loam/black soil are all genuine requirements.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements regarding temperate coniferous forest biome is not correct?
options: They are characterized by very little undergrowth.
They have a growing period of 50 to 100 days in a year.
There is low variation in annual temperature.
There is high range in spatial distribution of annual precipitation.
exp: The boreal/temperate coniferous (taiga) belt has very cold winters and mild summers, i.e. a large annual temperature range — so "low variation in annual temperature" is wrong. Sparse undergrowth and a short growing season are correct features.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following climatic types is found in Central Spain?
exp: Coastal Spain is Mediterranean, but the interior Meseta of central Spain is cut off from sea moisture and is semi-arid — a subtropical steppe. It is neither subarctic nor humid continental.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following Indian places receives minimum rainfall in a year?
exp: Leh lies in the cold desert of Ladakh, in the rain-shadow behind the high Himalayas, so it gets barely ~100 mm a year — far less than Jodhpur (Thar, ~360 mm), Delhi or Bengaluru.

subject: Geography
stem: Isohalines are lines joining equal
exp: "Iso-" means equal; isohalines join points of equal salinity (halos = salt). Equal-temperature lines are isotherms, equal-pressure are isobars, and equal-rainfall are isohyets.

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following statements about clouds:
exp: Clouds come in layered (stratiform) and heaped (cumuliform) forms (1) and are classed by height into high/middle/low (2); "nimbo/nimbus" marks rain-bearing clouds (4). Statement 3 is wrong — stratus, nimbostratus and stratocumulus are low clouds, not high. Hence 1, 2 and 4.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following pairs of Isolines and its properties are correctly matched?
exp: Isonif = equal snowfall (1), isohel = equal sunshine (2), isohaline = equal salinity (3). Statement 4 is wrong — an isohypse is a contour line of equal elevation/height, not cloudiness (equal cloudiness is an isoneph). Hence 1, 2 and 3.

2. Isohel - Sunshine
3. Isohaline - Salinity
4. Isohypse - Cloudiness

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the correct order of clouds in ascending order (lowest to highest) of height from surface?
exp: By base height: nimbostratus is a low cloud (2), altostratus is middle (4), and cirrocumulus and cirrus are high clouds, with cirrus highest (1 then 3). Lowest to highest = Nimbostratus, Altostratus, Cirrocumulus, Cirrus = 2, 4, 1, 3.

subject: Geography
stem: Identify the type of cloud on the basis of the given characteristics:
exp: High, thin, rippled patches of white ice-crystal cloud at great height, giving the "mackerel sky," are cirrocumulus. Altostratus/cirrostratus are sheet-like, and altocumulus form lower (middle level) and are made of water droplets.
subs: 1. High, thin, puffy white clouds of ice crystals that look like ripples
2. They appear between 20,000 feet and 40,000 feet above the Earth's surface
3. One of its types is called a "mackerel sky" because the clouds resemble largefish scales, especially when they are coloured pink at sunset
Select the correct answer:

subject: Geography
stem: How can one determine the relative humidity on a particular day at a given place?
options: If both temperature and absolute humidity are given
If percentage of absolute humidity is given
exp: Relative humidity = (actual water vapour ÷ the maximum the air can hold at that temperature) × 100. Since the air's holding capacity depends on temperature, you need both the absolute humidity and the temperature to compute it — one alone is not enough.

subject: Geography
stem: Cumulonimbus clouds develop from which among the following clouds?
exp: A cumulus cloud that keeps growing vertically becomes a towering cumulus congestus, which, with continued strong updrafts, builds into a cumulonimbus thunderstorm cloud. It does not grow out of the layered nimbostratus/altostratus or the high cirrocumulus.

subject: Geography
stem: Identify the cloud on the basis of the following characteristics relating to it
exp: "Cotton-wool" heaps with a distinct flat base are cumulus clouds (fair-weather, heaped, formed by convection). Cirrus are thin wispy ice clouds, stratus are featureless grey sheets, and nimbus are dark rain clouds — none match the cotton-wool, flat-based description.
subs: I. They look like cotton wool. II. They exist in patches and have at base. III. They are generally formed at a height of 4 to 7 km.
Select the answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists
exp: The Agulhas warms south-east Africa (2), the Humboldt (Peru) current cools the coast of Peru (1), the cold Labrador flows past Canada (4), and the cold Falkland runs along Argentina (3). So A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

A. Agulhas Current 1. Peru

subject: Geography
stem: The Gulf Stream is a poleward flowing current in the Atlantic Ocean. Which one of the following statements with regard to this is not correct?
options: It is similar to the Kuroshio current in the North pacific Ocean.
It transports warm, tropical water towards polar region.
This current is a major factor in weather along the east coast of the USA.
The warm water of the Gulf Stream sustains the coral reefs of West pacific Coast.
exp: The Gulf Stream is an Atlantic current, so it cannot sustain reefs on the West Pacific coast — that statement is false. It is indeed the Atlantic counterpart of the Kuroshio, carries warm water poleward (warming Western Europe), and shapes US east-coast weather.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not correct about Sargasso Sea?
options: It is characterized with anticyclonic circulation of ocean currents.
It records the highest salinity in Atlantic Ocean.
It is located west of Gulf Stream and east of Canary Current.
It is confined in gyre of calm and motionless water.
exp: The Sargasso Sea actually lies east of the Gulf Stream and west of the Canary Current (it sits inside the North Atlantic gyre) — statement c reverses this. Its anticyclonic gyre, high salinity and famously calm water are correctly described.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct?
exp: Visakhapatnam is a natural land-locked harbour sheltered by hills and a headland (1), and Deendayal (Kandla), in the Gulf of Kachchh, is a tidal port that depends on the high tide for ships to dock (2). Both are correct.
subs: 1. Visakhapatnam Port is a land-locked harbour.
2. Deendayal Port is a tidal port.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements concerning the natural vegetation of India is not correct?
options: Sal is found in moist deciduous forests.
Casuarina is largely found along the coastal region of Tamil Nadu.
Deodar is a coniferous species of tree.
Shola forests are found mainly on the upper reaches of Himalaya.
exp: Shola forests are montane temperate patches of the Western Ghats (Nilgiris/Anaimalai), not the Himalayas — so statement d is false. Sal (moist deciduous), coastal casuarina and the Himalayan conifer deodar are correctly described.

subject: Geography
stem: India signed an agreement in 2016 to develop a strategic port in one of its neighbouring countries. What is the name of the port?
exp: India agreed (2016) to develop Chabahar in Iran, giving sea access to Afghanistan and Central Asia while bypassing Pakistan. Gwadar (Pakistan) and Hambantota (Sri Lanka) are Chinese-built ports; Mongla is in Bangladesh.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not an exclusive right of the concerned coastal nations over Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)?
options: Survey and exploitation of mineral resources of ocean deposits
Exploitation of marine water energy and marine organisms including fishing
Conservation and management of marine resources
Navigation of ships and laying down submarine cables
exp: Within the EEZ the coastal state has exclusive rights to exploit and manage resources (minerals, fishing, energy). But navigation and the laying of submarine cables are freedoms open to all states (high-seas freedoms), not exclusive to the coastal nation.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements about India is not correct?
options: India has 12 major ports and about 200 non-major ports.
95 percent of India's trade by volume and 68 percent by value are moved through maritime transport.
India has a coastline of about 7500 km.
In the Maritime Agenda, 2010-2020, a target of 300 MT port capacity has been set for the year 2020.
exp: The Maritime Agenda 2010-2020 set a target of roughly 3,000+ MT (over 3 billion tonnes) of port capacity, not 300 MT — so this figure is far too low. The coastline (~7,517 km), the trade shares and the port count are correct.

subject: Geography
stem: Where is Hambantota Port located?
exp: Hambantota is a deep-water port on the southern coast of Sri Lanka, developed with Chinese assistance and later leased to a Chinese firm.

subject: Geography
stem: Recently islands of Andaman and Nicobar were connected with mainland by Submarine Optical Fibre Cable. Which one of the following islands was not connected initially?
exp: The CANI submarine cable (2020) linked Port Blair with islands such as Swaraj Dweep (Havelock), Little Andaman, Car Nicobar and Great Nicobar. Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island) was not among those connected in the initial rollout.

subject: Geography
stem: The Government wants to prepare a plan for drought prone areas of the country. Which one of the following regions will be predominantly focused?
exp: The arid Kutch region of Gujarat receives very little, erratic rainfall and is chronically drought-prone, so it would be a prime focus. Coastal Andhra, the well-watered Ganga plains and the high-rainfall North-East are not drought regions.

subject: Geography
stem: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many coastal and landlocked States of India, respectively?
exp: The Tropic of Cancer crosses 8 Indian States. Two are coastal (Gujarat and West Bengal) and six are landlocked (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Tripura, Mizoram) — so 2 and 6.

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following statements regarding transportation functions important ports
exp: Singapore both refuels/services passing ships (port of call) and re-exports goods (entrepôt) (1), and Karwar hosts INS Kadamba, a naval base (2). Statement 3 is wrong — Dover is a packet/ferry station, not an "outport" (an outport is a deep-water port built away from a silted parent port). Hence 1 and 2.
subs: 1. Singapore functions both as a port of call and an entrepot.
2. Karwar in India is an example of a naval port.
3. Dover in England is an example of an outport. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements regarding River Rhine is/are correct?
exp: Rotterdam sits at the Rhine–Meuse delta mouth and is Europe's busiest port (2, correct). Statement 1 is imprecise — the Rhine's great industrial belt (the Ruhr) is in western Germany, not "northern" Germany. (Some keys accept statement 1 loosely; the geography favours 2 only.)
subs: 1. Rhine River is an important pathway for industrial activity in northern Germany.
2. Port of Rotterdam is located at the mouth of the Rhine River.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following criteria are specified for granting Special Category Status to States in India?
exp: Special Category Status (Gadgil formula) considers hilly/difficult terrain (1), economic and infrastructural backwardness (2), a sizeable tribal population (4), low population density and a strategic location along international borders — not a coastal zone. So statement 3 is wrong; 1, 2 and 4 only.
subs: 1. Hilly and difficult terrain
2. Economic and infrastructural backwardness
3. Strategic coastal zone
4. Sizeable share of tribal population

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following statements with reference to location of Major Ports in India
exp: Cochin lies at the head of the Vembanad lagoon (2) and Mormugao at the Zuari estuary mouth in Goa (3) — both correct. Deendayal (Kandla) is on the Gulf of Kachchh, not Khambhat (1 wrong), and Paradip is on the Mahanadi delta, not the Godavari (4 wrong). Hence 2 and 3.
subs: 1. Deendayal Port is situated at the head of Gulf of Khambhat.
2. Cochin Port is situated at the head of Vembanad Kayal.
3. Mormugao Port is situated at the entrance of the Zuari estuary.
4. Paradip Port is situated in the Godavari delta. Which of the statements given above are correct?

subject: Geography
stem: Which one among the following is not a coral reef island?
exp: Kyushu is one of Japan's main volcanic islands, not a coral formation. The Great Barrier Reef, Fiji's Rainbow Reef and India's Swaraj (Havelock) Island are coral-reef sites.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of following is the most important factor for the formulation of smog?
options: Presence of many air pollutant resources
Rapid fall in temperature with increasing height above the sea level
exp: A temperature inversion (warm air sitting over cooler surface air) acts as a lid that traps pollutants and fog near the ground, concentrating them into smog. Pollutant sources and cold nights help, but without the trapping inversion the pollutants would simply disperse upward.

subject: Geography
stem: A biological community in its environment such as a pond, an ocean, a forest, even an aquarium is known as a
exp: An ecosystem is the living community plus its non-living environment interacting as a unit (energy flow, nutrient cycling). A biome is a large regional ecosystem type, a "community" is only the living part, and the abiotic environment is only the non-living part.

subject: Geography
stem: Timber vegetation is generally not found in which of the following regions?
exp: The tundra is too cold, with permafrost and a very short growing season, so trees cannot grow there (only mosses, lichens, low shrubs). Subtropical, temperate and (lower) alpine zones all support timber-yielding trees.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following countries does not have Tundra vegetation?
exp: Tundra occurs in high-latitude Arctic regions. The USA (Alaska), Russia (Siberia) and Canada all have extensive tundra, but Belarus lies in the temperate, forested belt of Europe and has none.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following land surfaces has the highest albedo?
exp: Albedo is the fraction of sunlight reflected. Fresh snow/ice reflects ~80–90% of incoming light (highest albedo), whereas rock, sand and dark vegetation absorb much more and reflect far less.

subject: Geography
stem: Which types of vegetation will youfind on the way as you travel from Bikaner to Konark by road by shortest distance?
options: Tropical thorny, Desert, Moist deciduous, Mangrove
Desert, Tropical thorny, Moist deciduous, Mangrove
Moist deciduous, Tropical thorny, Mangrove, Desert
Desert, Tropical thorny, Mangrove, Moist deciduous
exp: Going west-to-east from Bikaner (Thar) to Konark (Odisha coast), rainfall rises steadily: desert scrub → tropical thorny → moist deciduous forest → coastal mangroves at the delta. Option b matches this natural moisture gradient.

subject: Geography
stem: Energy and nutrients flow from one trophic level to another in an ecosystem. Which one of the following statements correctly describes the direction of flow of energy and nutrients in an ecosystem?
options: Energy flow is cyclic and nutrient flow is unidirectional.
Energy flow is unidirectional and nutrient flow is cyclic.
Both energy and nutrient flow are unidirectional.
Both energy and nutrient flow are cyclic.
exp: Energy enters as sunlight and is progressively lost as heat at each trophic level, so it flows one way and is not reused. Nutrients (carbon, nitrogen, etc.) are recycled repeatedly between organisms and the environment — so nutrient flow is cyclic.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one among the following is not a feature of Xerophytes?
exp: Xerophytes are adapted to conserve water, so they have fewer stomata (often sunken in pits), small leaves and a thick waxy cuticle to cut transpiration. A "large number of stomata" would increase water loss — the opposite of a xerophytic trait.

subject: Geography
stem: Halophytes are the plants that grow on which one among the following categories of soil?
exp: Halophytes (e.g. mangroves, salt-marsh plants) are specially adapted to tolerate high salt concentrations, so they grow on saline soils of coasts, estuaries and salt flats.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is correct?
options: Guindy National Park is known for tiger reserve.
Namdapha National Park is meant for lion conservation.
Rann of Kutch is a Wild Ass Sanctuary.
exp: The Little Rann of Kutch hosts the Wild Ass (Ghudkhur) Sanctuary — the last refuge of the Indian wild ass (d correct). Guindy is a small city park (not a tiger reserve), Namdapha is tiger/biodiversity habitat (not lions), and Jaldapara is a wildlife sanctuary/park, not a biosphere reserve.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not a biosphere reserve of India?
exp: The Great Himalayan is a National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), not a biosphere reserve. Agasthyamalai, Nokrek and Great Nicobar are designated biosphere reserves.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following National Parks of India are declared as World Heritage by UNESCO?
exp: Keoladeo (Bharatpur), Sundarbans and Kaziranga are inscribed UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Ranthambore is a famous tiger reserve but is not a World Heritage Site, so it is excluded — 1, 2 and 3 only.
subs: 1. Keoladeo National Park
2. Sundarbans National Park
3. Kaziranga National Park
4. Ranthambore National Park
Select the correct answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following viruses is responsible for the recent death of lions in Gir National Park?
exp: The 2018 deaths of Asiatic lions in Gir were linked mainly to Canine Distemper Virus (along with babesiosis), a disease that can jump from dogs to big cats. Nipah, Hendra and Foot-and-Mouth viruses were not responsible.

subject: Geography
stem: In the year 2020 which one of the following tiger reserves of India was declared by UNESCO as a Biosphere Reserve?
exp: Panna (Madhya Pradesh) — famous for its successful tiger-reintroduction programme — was added to UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere network in 2020.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following biosphere reserves comprises islands with estuaries, beaches, coral reefs, salt marshes and mangroves?
exp: The Gulf of Mannar marine biosphere reserve contains a chain of islands with coral reefs, seagrass, mangroves, salt marshes and beaches. Sunderban lacks coral reefs, while Nilgiri and Nanda Devi are inland (terrestrial) reserves.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following about Khijadiya Bird Sanctuary is/are correct?
exp: Khijadiya was declared a Ramsar wetland of international importance (1, correct), but it is in Gujarat (near Jamnagar), not Uttar Pradesh — so statement 2 is wrong. Hence 1 only.
subs: 1. It is recently declared as a Ramsar Site (wetlands of international importance)
2. It is located in Uttar Pradesh
Select the correct answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: With reference to Bhindawas Wildlife Sanctuary, Sultanpur National Park, Thol Lake Wildlife Sanctuary and Wadhwana Wetland, which of the following statements is/are correct?
exp: All four are Ramsar sites (1) and important bird habitats (3). Statement 2 is wrong — several are man-made (Bhindawas and Wadhwana are reservoirs, Sultanpur a managed wetland), not naturally formed. Hence 1 and 3 only.
subs: 1. All of them are Ramsar sites.
2. All of them are naturally formed wetlands.
3. All of them are birding sites.
Select the correct answer using the code given below

subject: Geography
stem: The Ramsar Convention relates to which one of the following areas?
exp: The Ramsar Convention (1971, signed in Ramsar, Iran) is the international treaty for the conservation and "wise use" of wetlands. Afforestation, climate change and desertification are covered by other agreements.

subject: Geography
stem: Cheetahs, brought from Namibia, were introduced in India to which one of the following National Parks?
exp: Under Project Cheetah (2022), African cheetahs from Namibia (and later South Africa) were released in Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh, chosen for its suitable grassland-savanna habitat.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
exp: "Kanke" is associated with Ranchi, Jharkhand, not Arunachal Pradesh — so this pair is wrong. Ramnagar (Uttarakhand), Chakrashila (Assam) and Nahar (Haryana) are correctly matched.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following Ramsar Wetland sites is not situated in any of the Union Territories of India?
options: Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary
exp: Point Calimere is in Tamil Nadu, a State — not a UT. Hokera and Wular are in the UT of Jammu & Kashmir, and Tsomoriri is in the UT of Ladakh. So Point Calimere is the odd one out.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements about Nilgiri, Surat and Vaghsheer is correct?
options: These are Tiger Reserves in the state of Gujarat.
These are combatants commissioned by the Indian Navy.
These are Biodiversity parks maintained by the Indian Army.
These are Tiger Reserves maintained by the Indian Navy.
exp: Nilgiri (stealth frigate), Surat (destroyer) and Vagsheer (Scorpène-class submarine) are warships/combatants of the Indian Navy, not tiger reserves or parks.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following air pollutants combines with the haemoglobin of human blood and reduces its oxygen-carrying capacity, leading to suffocation and may cause even death?
exp: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin far more strongly than oxygen (forming carboxyhaemoglobin), so the blood can no longer carry enough oxygen — leading to suffocation. CFCs, fly ash and SO₂ harm health by other mechanisms, not by this haemoglobin binding.

subject: Geography
stem: What are the main constituents of biogas?
exp: Biogas, produced by the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter, is mainly methane (~55–70%) with carbon dioxide, plus traces of other gases. The other options wrongly list SO₂, nitric oxide or hydrogen as main components.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not included in the National Air Quality Index?
exp: India's National AQI tracks PM2.5, PM10, SO₂, NO₂, CO, ozone, ammonia and lead. Methane is a greenhouse gas but is not one of the eight AQI pollutants.

subject: Geography
stem: The Basel Convention is aimed at protecting human health and environment against adverse effects of which of the following?
exp: The Basel Convention controls the transboundary movement and disposal of hazardous wastes. POPs are covered by the Stockholm Convention, mercury by the Minamata Convention, and chemicals/pesticides trade by the Rotterdam Convention.

subject: Geography
stem: One carbon credit is accepted as equivalent to
exp: One carbon credit represents one tonne (1,000 kg) of CO₂ (or CO₂-equivalent) reduced, avoided or removed. The smaller figures and the "carbon" (rather than CO₂) options are incorrect.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements about the Global Environment Facility Grant Agreement, signed by India in August 2017 with the World Bank for Ecosystems Service Improvement Project, is not correct?
options: The size of the project is about USD 25 million.
The duration of the project is 15 years.
The project will entirely be nanced by the World Bank out of its GEF Trust Fund.
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change will implement the project.
exp: The project ran for about five years, not 15 — so this statement is wrong. The ~USD 24–25 million size, GEF Trust Fund financing and MoEFCC implementation are correct.

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following statements about National Wildlife Action Plan (NWAP) of India for 2017-2031
exp: NWAP 2017-2031 is indeed India's Third action plan (1) and the first to formally address climate-change impacts on wildlife (2). The "ten components" figure (3) is not accurate, so 1 and 2 only.
subs: 1. This is the Third National Wildlife Action Plan.
2. The NWAP is unique as this is the first time India has recognized the concerns relating to climate change impact on wildlife.
3. The NWAP has ten components. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements about the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change is not correct?
options: The fund is meant to assist national and State level activities to meet the cost of adaptation measures.
This scheme has been taken as a Central Sector Scheme.
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research is the national implementing entity for the fund.
The scheme has been in force since 2015-2016.
exp: The National Implementing Entity for the NAFCC is NABARD, not the ICAR — so statement c is wrong. Its purpose (funding adaptation), its Central-Sector status and its 2015-16 launch are correct.

subject: Geography
stem: The Kyoto Protocol is an international treaty that commits State parties to reduction in
exp: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) bound industrialised nations to legally binding cuts in greenhouse-gas emissions. It has nothing to do with poverty, nuclear arms or farm subsidies.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the nodal agency in India for the United Nations Environment Programme?
options: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
The Ministry of Science and Technology
exp: The MoEFCC is India's nodal ministry for UNEP and most international environmental conventions. The others handle different portfolios.

subject: Geography
stem: The National Disaster Management Authority functions under the Ministry of
exp: The NDMA (chaired by the Prime Minister) works under the Ministry of Home Affairs, which handles internal security and disaster management.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements about National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) with reference to India is/are correct?
exp: The NAPCC does argue that sustained high growth is needed to raise living standards and reduce vulnerability (1, correct). But it was released in 2008, not 2014 — so statement 2 is wrong. Hence 1 only.
subs: 1. It emphasises that maintaining a high growth rate is essential for raising the living standards of the vast majority of the people of India and reducing their vulnerability to the impact of climate change.
2. It was released in 2014.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements about Green Credit Initiative is/are correct?
exp: The Green Credit Initiative is a market-based response to climate change (1) that rewards environment-positive actions like tree planting on degraded land and river catchments (2). Statement 3 (replacing kerosene with solar) describes a different scheme, so 1 and 2 only.
subs: 1. It is a response to the challenge of climate change.
2. It promotes plantations on wasteland and river catchment areas.
3. It is a scheme of the Government of India to replace the kerosene oil with solar power used by the rural poor.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: SAGAR-SETU is a mobile app, which aims to improve the Ease of Doing Business.
Harit Sagar aims at achieving Zero Carbon Emission Goal.
Sagar Manthan is a mission launched by Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Government of India, to increase fish production.
Costa Serena is the first international cruise liner in India.
exp: Sagar Manthan is the Mercantile Marine Domain Awareness Centre — a real-time maritime data/monitoring dashboard of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, not a fish-production mission. The other statements are correct.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following statements about the National Green Tribunal is not correct?
options: It was set up in the year 2010.
It is involved in effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests.
It may consider giving relief and compensation for damages to persons and property.
It is bound by the procedures laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
exp: The NGT is not bound by the rigid procedures of the CPC (or the Evidence Act); it follows the principles of natural justice for speedy environmental justice — so statement d is wrong. Its 2010 establishment, mandate and power to award compensation are correct.

subject: Geography
stem: Why was Dholavira in the news recently?
options: For the discovery of gold and precious stones at this site
It received the UNESCO World Heritage Tag
exp: Dholavira, a Harappan city in Gujarat's Rann of Kutch known for its water management, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021 — the reason it was in the news.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements about Marrakech Partnership is/are correct?
exp: The Marrakech Partnership for Global Climate Action (launched 2016) connects governments with non-state actors to implement the Paris Agreement — exactly what statement 2 says. Statement 1 is incomplete/incorrect (it is not purely intergovernmental), and statement 3 misattributes its guiding framework (it supports the Paris Agreement). Hence 2 only.
subs: 1. It is an intergovernmental partnership for global climate action.
2. It is not only an intergovernmental partnership for global climate action but also a collaboration between governments and other stakeholders like cities, businesses and investors.
3. This partnership is guided by the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

exp: These are power-project sites: Satpura thermal plant in Madhya Pradesh (4), Dhuvaran thermal plant in Gujarat (3), Tanakpur hydel project in Uttarakhand (2), and Dabhol power plant in Maharashtra (1). So A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1.

4. Madhya
D. Dabhol Pradesh

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the highest altitude zoo in the world?
options: Pandit G. B. Pant High Altitude Zoo
exp: The Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park at Darjeeling (~2,150 m) is India's highest-altitude zoo, noted for breeding the red panda and snow leopard. The others are at lower elevations (or, in Cheyenne's case, in the USA).

subject: Geography
stem: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists
exp: Anaimudi (highest peak of South India) is in the Annamalai/Anaimalai hills (4); Doddabetta is the highest of the Nilgiris (1); Dhupgarh is the highest of the Satpura (Mahadeo) range (2); Guru Shikhar is the highest of the Aravalli (Mt Abu) (3). So A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3.
