subject: Geography
stem: In which one of the following highlands of India can youfind temperate forests called Sholas?
exp: Sholas are patches of stunted temperate evergreen forest growing in the moist valleys/folds of the high Western Ghats, especially the Nilgiris, interspersed with grassland. They are not a Vindhya, Satpura or Himalayan feature.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following passes is not located in Indian Himalayan region?
exp: The Bolan Pass is in Balochistan, Pakistan (a historic gateway to Afghanistan), not the Indian Himalayas. Zojila (Ladakh), Shipki La (Himachal) and Lipulekh (Uttarakhand) are Indian Himalayan passes.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following set of trees does not belong to Temperate Floral Zone of Himalaya?
exp: The temperate Himalayan zone has oak, maple, rhododendron, birch and laurel. Cashewnut is a tropical lowland/coastal tree, so a "cashewnut" set does not belong to the temperate Himalayan flora.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following biosphere reserves is spread over three States in India?
exp: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve spreads across three States — Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka. Achanakmar-Amarkantak spans only two States; Seshachalam and Agasthyamalai lie within single States.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one among the following Biosphere Reserves is spread over three states in India?
exp: Again, the Nilgiri reserve covers Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka. Dehang Debang and Nokrek lie within single north-eastern States, and Seshachalam is within Andhra Pradesh.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one among the following tributaries of Indus River does not originate in the Himalayas?
exp: The Gomal (Gumal) rises in the Sulaiman Range of Afghanistan/Pakistan, west of the Indus — not in the Himalayas. The Gilgit, Hunza and Zaskar all rise in the Himalayan/Karakoram system.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is not a tributary of the river Ganga?
exp: The Teesta drains Sikkim/North Bengal and joins the Brahmaputra (in Bangladesh), not the Ganga. The Son, Mahananda and Sharada (Sarda) are all part of the Ganga system.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of occurrences of rivers from Chennai to Kolkata when travelled by road (shortest distance)?
exp: Going north up the east coast from Chennai you cross the Penner (Penneru) first, then the Godavari, Mahanadi and Subarnarekha before Kolkata — the order in option b. The Kaveri lies south of Chennai (so you would not cross it), ruling out option a; the others jumble the north-to-south order.

subject: Geography
stem: Which river is praised in the fth century Tamil epic, Silappadikaram?
exp: The Tamil epic Silappadikaram glorifies the Cauvery (Kaveri), the lifeline river of the Chola heartland. The Godavari, Saraswati and Ganges are not the river celebrated in it.

subject: Geography
stem: Consider the following tributaries of river Ganga
exp: From east to west along the Ganga plain the left-bank tributaries occur as Kosi → Gandak → Ghaghara → Gomti = 2, 1, 3, 4 (the Kosi joins farthest east in Bihar, the Gomti farthest west in UP).
subs: 1. Gandak
2. Kosi
3. Ghaghara
4. Gomti Which one of the following is the correct order of the above rivers from east to west?

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is a west- owing river?
exp: The Narmada flows westward through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges into the Arabian Sea. The Mahanadi, Godavari and Krishna all flow east into the Bay of Bengal.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one among the following is not a tributary of river Luni?
exp: The Luni (Rajasthan's main river) is fed by the Sukri, Jawai and Khari. The Banas is a tributary of the Chambal (Yamuna system), not the Luni. (Note: a separate "West Banas" exists, but the Banas of the Chambal is intended.)

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following rivers takes a U turn at Namcha Barwa and enters India?
exp: The Brahmaputra (Tsangpo in Tibet) loops sharply around the peak Namcha Barwa in the "Great Bend," then turns south to enter Arunachal Pradesh. The other rivers do not make this turn.

subject: Geography
stem: Where are the largest quantity of cichlids found in India?
exp: Cichlid fish (such as the pearlspot/karimeen) thrive in the brackish backwaters of Kerala, a noted habitat. The Sundarbans, Narmada and Godavari are not the chief cichlid waters.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following rivers joins Ganga directly?
exp: The Son is a major right-bank tributary that joins the Ganga directly (near Patna). The Chambal, Betwa and Ken all flow into the Yamuna, which then joins the Ganga.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following tributaries of river Indus feeds the canal system of the Bhakra Nangal Project?
exp: The Bhakra-Nangal project is built on the Satluj (Sutlej), whose stored water feeds its extensive canal network in Punjab/Haryana. The Chenab, Ravi and Jhelum are separate Indus tributaries.

subject: Geography
stem: D performs her train journey by the shortest route from Bengaluru to New Delhi. Which one of the following rivers will she not cross while performing the journey?
exp: On the shortest Bengaluru–Delhi route (via Hyderabad–Nagpur–Bhopal–Agra) you cross the Krishna, Godavari and Narmada, but the road stays largely west of the Yamuna, reaching Delhi without crossing it. So the Yamuna is the one not crossed.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the first and the oldest Government-owned coal mining company in India?
exp: Singareni Collieries (founded 1920, now jointly owned by Telangana and the Centre) is India's oldest government coal company. Coal India Ltd (1975), NLC and Mahanadi Coalfields are all younger.

subject: Geography
stem: On the banks of which one of the following rivers was the ancient Mahishmati located?
exp: Mahishmati, an ancient capital (associated with the Haihaya/Avanti region and later the Kalachuris), stood on the Narmada. It was not on the Sarayu, Son or Godavari.

subject: Geography
stem: What will be the correct sequence of cities on the bank of river Ganga if someone moves from west to east?
exp: West to east the true order is Kanpur → Prayagraj → Patna → Bhagalpur. Option c starts correctly (Kanpur, Prayagraj) and is the best available, but as printed it places Bhagalpur before Patna — a transcription slip (Patna actually lies west of Bhagalpur). Treat (c) as the intended answer.

subject: Geography
stem: Indus river basin is extended up to
options: Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab
Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana
Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan
Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan
exp: Through its tributaries (especially the Sutlej system), the Indus basin in India reaches across Ladakh, Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan. The shorter lists omit states the basin actually covers.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct?
exp: The Bakhshali Manuscript is an early mathematical text covering fractions, roots and progressions (1), and Aryabhata computed pi ≈ 3.1416 (2). Statement 3 is wrong — the Sharangadhara Samhita is a medieval medical (Ayurvedic) text, not a treatise on polity. Hence 1 and 2 only.
subs: 1. The Bakshali Manuscript written in the Gatha language (a refined version of old Prakrit) using the Sharada script deals with topics such as fractions, square roots, arithmetic and geometric progressions.
2. In the field of geometry, Aryabhatta described the various properties of a circle giving a very accurate value for pi (correct to four decimal places) at 3.1416.
3. Sharangadhara Samhita is an important text on political system of ancient India.

stem: Under which one of the following rivers has India'sfirst underwater metro rail tunnel been constructed?
exp: India's first under-river metro tunnel runs beneath the Hooghly in Kolkata (the East-West Metro), connecting Howrah with the city. It is not under the Yamuna, Ganga or Gomti.

subject: Geography
stem: On which among the following is National Waterway No. 2 situated?

subject: Geography
stem: Alluvial soils vary in nature from sandy loam to clay. They are generally
options: poor in potash and rich in phosphorus.
poor in both potash and phosphorus.
rich in both potash and phosphorus.
rich in potash and poor in phosphorus.
exp: Indian alluvial soils are typically rich in potash but poor in phosphorus (and nitrogen and humus). The other combinations misstate this nutrient balance.

subject: Geography
stem: Identify the type of soil on the basis of given characteristics:

2. Their structure ranges from sandy to loamy.

stem: Consider the following statements

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following groups of cities does not have Sclerophyll as its natural vegetation cover?

Las Vegas (hot desert) and Queensland (humid tropical/subtropical) are not Mediterranean, so they lack sclerophyll.

subject: Geography
stem: The ratio of gross cropped area to the net sown area is called
exp: Cropping intensity = (gross cropped area ÷ net sown area) × 100; it shows how many times the same land is cropped in a year (multiple cropping raises it above 100%). The other terms measure rotation, output per hectare, or variety of crops.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following crops is not cultivated in Karewas, the lacustrine deposits of sand, clay, loam, silt and boulders?

subject: Geography
stem: Milpa and Ladang are different names for
exp: Milpa (Mexico/Central America) and Ladang (Southeast Asia) are local terms for shifting (slash-and-burn) cultivation, where forest is cleared and burned, cropped for a few years, then abandoned. They are not mixed, truck or plantation farming.

subject: Geography
stem: Identify the crop on the basis of the following characteristics:

subs: 1. It is a kharif crop.
2. Aus, Aman and Boro are its three different growing periods in an agricultural year.
3. About one-fourth of the total cropped area of India is under its cultivation.

subject: Geography

subject: Geography
stem: The phenomenon of demographic dividend of a country relates to
options: a sharp decline in total population
an increase in working age population
a decline in infant mortality rate
exp: The demographic dividend is the economic boost a country gets when the share of working-age people (15–64) is large relative to dependants, providing more workers and savings. It is not about falling total population, infant mortality or sex ratio.

subject: Geography

stem: Which one of the following statements regarding sex composition is not correct?

subject: Geography
stem: What do you mean by Demographic Dividend?
options: A rise in the rate of economic growth due to a higher share of working age people in a population
A rise in the rate of literacy due to development of educational institutions in different parts of the country
A rise in the standard of living of the people due to the growth of alternative livelihood practices
A rise in the gross employment ratio of a country due to government policies
exp: The demographic dividend is the lift to economic growth that comes when a larger proportion of the population is of working age. The other options describe literacy, living standards or employment policy, not the dividend itself.

subject: Geography

stem: According to the Census 2011, in India, what is the percentage of people approximately to be considered migrants (internal, i.e., now settled in a place different from their previous residence)?

subject: Geography
stem: Decadal growth rate of population in percentage was highest in India in the year
exp: The highest decadal growth (~24.8% for 1961-71) was recorded at the 1971 Census — the peak of India's population-growth rate. Later censuses (1981 onward) show a declining rate.

subject: Geography
stem: In a discussion, M from Arunachal Pradesh, J from Assam, N from Meghalaya and S from Nagaland are claiming that as per Census 2011, their State has the maximum density of population. Identify the person making the correct claim.

subject: Geography
stem: In India, the period of steady population growth refers to the decades of

subject: Geography
stem: If it is 1000 a.m. at Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), then what will be the time at 90�E longitude?
